---
title: "NCDB Research Guide"
---


A practical learning path from your first research question to a reproducible analysis. You do not need NCDB access or prior Python experience to begin.

## Begin with the foundations

| Order | Lesson | What you will leave with |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Start Here: What is NCDB?](start_here.qmd) | A feasible question and a clear description of the population |
| 2 | [Obtaining Access](access.qmd) | An application preparation checklist and a local approvals record |
| 3 | [The PUF and downloaded files](puf.qmd) | A release inventory and a safe storage plan |
| 4 | [Navigating the Data Dictionary](dictionary.qmd) | Your first documented variable-map entry |
| 5 | [Coding Systems](coding_systems.qmd) | A plan for checking site, histology, stage, and year-specific coding |
| 6 | [Computer, VS Code, and Python Setup](setup.qmd) | A working environment and a successful synthetic practice run |

Read these six lessons in order. Each includes a practice task and a readiness check. Use the sidebar to move between lessons or search for a term such as “unknown,” “PUF,” or “clinical stage.”

## Choose your next step

**Still waiting for access?** Complete the foundations and [synthetic walkthrough](synthetic.qmd). All practice records are invented.

**Have approved data?** Start with the [import plan](import.qmd), [variable map](dictionary.qmd), and [cohort definition](cohort.qmd). Keep records in approved institutional storage outside this guide.

**Ready to analyze?** Use the [analysis overview](analysis.qmd) to select a method with your mentor. The later chapters are introductory checklists and the scripts are teaching components, not a validated end-to-end NCDB analysis pipeline.

**Preparing a manuscript?** Review [pitfalls](pitfalls.qmd), [reporting](manuscript.qmd), and [reproducibility and handoff](reproducibility.qmd).

## How to read this guide

::: {.callout-note title="Official source — verify against your release"}
Links point to ACS/NCDB or other responsible organizations. Source summaries are original paraphrases, not a replacement for the applicable dictionary, manual, or agreement. Public sources were checked on September 7, 2026; requirements may change. See the [source register](sources.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Educational explanation"}
Our explanations and fictional examples help you learn the workflow. They do not establish official code meanings or clinical conclusions.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Project decision — document and review"}
Eligibility rules, study years, confounders, missing-data methods, model specification, and disclosure review belong to your study protocol. Record who approved each decision and why.
:::

## Data Privacy and Security

This repository holds code, original teaching material, and synthetic examples only. No real records or data are included here. Never copy patient data, screenshots of records, model prediction files, credentials, or restricted downloads. This guide is meant to be an introduction with theoretical examples only. Read [data protection](data_protection.qmd) before working with approved records.

## Development status

The six foundation lessons and synthetic workflow are developed for onboarding. Advanced lessons remain explicitly marked teaching outlines. They cover the intended full workflow but still need site-specific examples, expert methodological review, and expanded exercises before serving as a comprehensive analysis curriculum.
